# How to bleed air from a hydronic radiator

If your radiator gets warm at the bottom but stays cold at the top, there's trapped air inside it,
and bleeding it will usually fix the problem in a few minutes.

## What you'll need

Grab a radiator key (sold at any hardware store for a couple of dollars), a small cloth or towel,
and a shallow container to catch drips. Turn off your heating system before you start, and give the
radiators about twenty minutes to cool if they've been running.

## Steps

1. Find the bleed valve, a small square-ish fitting near the top of one end of the radiator.
2. Hold the cloth underneath it to catch any water that escapes once air starts venting.
3. Fit the radiator key onto the fitting and turn it counterclockwise, about a quarter turn.
4. Listen for a hissing sound; that's the trapped air escaping through the open valve.
5. Once the hissing stops and a small stream of water starts coming out steadily, close it again
   by turning the key clockwise until it stops.
6. Repeat this on every unit in the house, starting with whichever one is lowest in the system
   and working your way up to the highest floor.

## After you're done

Check your boiler's pressure gauge once you've bled every radiator, since removing air usually drops
the reading a little. Most home boilers have a filling loop you can open briefly to top the level
back up to the mark on the gauge. Turn your heating back on and give it half an
hour; the units that were cold at the top should now heat evenly from end to end.

If a radiator still won't heat evenly after bleeding, the valve on that unit may need adjustment, or
there may be a blockage worth asking a plumber to look at.
